text:
Yes, this is likely the reason behind the release.

To be able to better use the NAVI chip stock with bad CUs but still passing the high speed clock test.

That's all.  This is why often the second-highest tier is released (full die) then the ones under it.  Then higher clocked variants of the ones under it, and finally the top line with the select full dies.  

Occasionally, if they delay release long enough they can have enough full dies with high clock rates to get a top clock model available in limited quantities at release.   However, they will never have a top clock model of the cut reject dies at release, because testing resources beyond the basic A/B binning of potential top tier chips are dedicated to the full die chips.

text:
A few months ago I upgraded from a 1050 ti to a 6700 xt. I chose this the 6700 xt because I saw many reviewers recommend this card. 
The graphics are amazing. Fps is amazing. Temperatures are amazing. The quiet fans are amazing. I love the amd control panel.
BUT, This is why I would NOT recommend my video card. I have a sound issue since day one. The sound in games will cut off and on 30 to 50 times a minute when it's bad and only up to 15 to 30 times a minute when it's better. Sometimes it will happen several times while just watching a video other times it won't.  I searched the problem and found it to be kind of wide spread. If a youtuber doesn't experience an issue with a part then they are oblivious and proceed to recommend it. They never research possible problems with a part before recommending it. This is why you shouldn't take recommendations from a small collection of "reputable" reviewers. The sound issue is widespread and has been around since before the 6000 series. It is not all models and not all 6700 xt, but it is spread over multiple brands. Since this is a widespread and long lived issue AMD has been well aware of it yet has not fixed it. I also believe that AMD will never fix it because they either can't or won't. I believe this because the problem is not listed anywhere on their website as a known issue and it is no where to be found in their support or forums yet I've posts everywhere else on the internet about it. 
I've tried every potential "fix" that have worked for others I could find on the internet and there are many. I am not a pc novice. I am very comfortable with using ddu and installing drivers properly. With the internet disconnected to prevent Windows from downloading more drivers, I've clean out all brands of audio and video drivers from my system and disabled the other devices in the device manager as well. I've tried other reported fixes such as resolution changes, overclocking and underclocking the card, changing sample rates and bit depths and exclusive control settings, changed to better hdmi cables, some registry tweaks, tested power supply, tested pc ram, etc. etc. etc. Sometimes the fixes seem to improve the problem for a while but not for long. Someone asked why I don't just connect the pc built in audio and forget about it. Sure, I did. I had to do it because the sound issue is like like chinese water torture. I bought new ten foot audio cables and connected them. But why should I have to do that and why should I have to forget about it? I had absolutely zero sound issues with my little old 1050 ti. It just worked. It even still worked pretty darn good when I was too lazy from time to time to clean install new drivers. I don't want to have to pay Nvidia hundreds more dollars for the same performance. Oddly everyone seems to agree that the cards themselves are not defective. I don't know if the issue is compression, codecs, acceleration, conflict with windows, conflict with other hardware, or something else. If someone has a fix for this issue I please respond. I was set to become an AMD fan boy too, but at this time I cannot recommend AMD to anyone.
author: @havocstormbringer1503

text: @iamspencerx  My temporary solution has been this. Every one to two weeks I clean reinstall my sound driver. That makes it good, but slowly gets worse over time. When it becomes too much I reinstall. That to me doesn't sound like a new cable is needed. That's seem like perhaps a memory leak. That's my uneducated guess

author: @Born_Stellar

text:
@Born_Stellar  that's all relative. Just cuz something CAN handle heat doesn't mean it should. An engine is capable of hitting coolant temperatures of around 270 until IMMEDIATE thermal related failures, but above 230 you start risking blowing out hose, old gaskets (including head gaskets), warping surfaces (manifolds, heads, etc). 

It's called thermal fatigue. The more heating and cooling cycles an object goes through, the quicker it wears out. The hotter it gets during said cycles, it fatigues even quicker.

That 120⁰ is more than likely the fairly immediate failure point. In the case of my RX580, every source is saying to keep it between 75 and 85 max, anything above 90 starts to degrade the card. Even looking at how AMD designed the thing: it starts thermal throttling at 80⁰. Now if a manufacturer makes something begin to severely regulate itself above a certain temperature, it's a clear indication that said something is not meant to run above that temperature.

All said and done, I'd rather not have an oven of a PC, especially since my new processor runs at 70-80 under load even after adding 3 case fans and an aftermarket cooler. If I were to run the 6700xt, which runs an average of 15-20⁰ hotter than the 3070 I got, those temps would only be exacerbated.

text: Nvidia has a better product overall this generation. I'm not a fanboy. My main rig is a 5900X/6800XT and my travel mini-ITX rig is a 5600x/6700xt. AMD cards have great rasterization performance. I don't care about ray tracing, but many do and Nvidia's ray tracing performs better in today's games. Raytracing causes too much of a performance hit... even on Nvidia's cards... to make it worth while IMO. Nvidia's killer feature is DLSS which will only improve with time. AMD's counter is interesting but not as effective or as widely implemented. It's also not unique to AMD cards. Nvidia's nvenc encoder is also ahead of AMD's implementation. If I was willing to pay above MSRP, I likely would have chosen the RTX 3080 and RTX 3060Ti respectively. I was able to get both of my cards from AMD directly for MSRP. I'm happy with my purchases, but AMD needs to improve their features if they truly wish to compete with Nvidia.
author: @PoppaCYS

text:
@PoppaCYS  Upscaling is not a feature. It was a bubblegum and duct tape workaround nVidia had to do because even with RT cores their realtime raytracing was literally unplayable even with a 2080ti. The 2080ti got like 30fps at 1080p without it. That is the sole reason DLSS even exists, and somehow they found a way of deluding people into thinking their janky hack workaround was itself a "feature." Then you go and look at the DLSS you got and it was fucking dog shit. Not that any of this mattered because in the end it was as relevant as Hairworks.

Yeah. You guys remember that right? How we all should've gotten a Pascal card because AMD didn't have HairWorks, right?

Yeah no people got Pascal cards because we care about performance and how much that performance is going to cost us. In RTX series case it's abysmally poor performance uplift, if any at all. Even MSRP it's garbage. Even MSRP is going from already ripoff tier $500 MSRP for 2070 super to $600 3070ti that is straight up inferior performing to a cheaper AMD card. All the while they're effectively trying to find ways of shadowbanning reviewers for not putting RT front and center along with their other gimmicks because unlike Pascal they can't actually stand on their performance anymore, and the gimmicks themselves still don't matter two generations later because of how few games even have RT as an option to begin with.

I've got 500 games and I've searched through all those game libraries and then added games I might buy on top of it and came up with a whopping 5 games wishlisted or bought that have RT or something. It's as irrelevant to me as FSR. It's like trying to sell an entire game based on some neat easter egg in an obscure hidden location. Dude, if the game sucks I don't care about your easter egg. In this case everything about Ampere is just shit to me, and it sucks harder because it drags the pricing trend to where nVidia wants it which is a low end GPU costing as much as a used car for some loud, hot, Soviet industrial machinery tier inefficient crap with a green logo on it.

So in short, no, I am absolutely not paying fucking double to make some lights impercitibly shinier on Amid Evil. It's completely irrelevant to me as a gamer, and that's why I ended up not getting Turing. To me it's like "well AMD has raytracing so it's a box ticked I guess" in the same way that resizable BAR or something is, or going "oh this board can do CrossFire and SLI ok" like would you buy a $400 board just because it had SLI as a feature? That's how I feel about it, and as I accurately predicted in 2019 there wouldn't be even be enough games to make it a consideration until RDNA3/Lovelace came out. 

But to really harp on this, no, an upscaler is not a feature, and it was the sole way they could even try to make a $1200 card that could only get 30fps at 1080p with their prized feature look attractive to anyone. They did this in spite of the fact DLSS 1.0 was such horrible trash that to get prettier lights and reflections with RT you'd have to utterly destroy your FPS and to fix your ruined FPS now have to slap on some completely ugly vaseline upscaler which eventually defeats the whole original purpose. Now they try and say "yeah but DLSS 2.0 is so much better than 1.0!" So? That's like telling me your prebuilt is better than Dell. You're not saying much with that.

All I care about is raw performance. The fact the companies have tried shifting the entire conversation away from what has been the fundamental metric for 20 years now is saying something fundamentally rotten to me about how bottomed out they are that they're effectively trying to say "performance doesn't matter, only proprietary FeaturesTM matters" I expect to upgrade to a card that can run 4K natively and hopefully hit 144hz 4k in a couple years. Like I said elsewhere, you'll see how pointless DLSS is and how hard DLSS and FSR gets dropped once we have those cards running high refresh 4K native, when the literal entire point of 4K is maximum fidelity, and RT on top of it is also about fidelity so clearly that very expensive autistic obsession with fidelity is going to make any upscaler unattractive. RT is not there yet. It eventually probably will be, but considering that and DLSS aren't even options in literally 99.9% of games I do or would play makes it not even a consideration to me when purchasing hardware.

If it is to you then you do you man it's your money, but I'm just saying, these MSRPs are absolute bullshit and to me so are the alleged features and the performance. This is partly why if I were building now the only card I'd even vaguely consider is 3070, and only if the AIB cards aren't so ridiculously expensive that I'd might as well just get a 6800XT instead, which is pretty much what happened last year. I was angling for a 2070 super, and then I realized what year it is and that I didn't care about  2070s having SLI as a FeatureTM, realized I wouldn't care about RT even if I had games that had it, realized it wasn't strong enough for RT on my 1440p display anyway, and eventually realized the competitor was similar performing and massively more aesthetically pleasing (Taichi) and I'd get about the same thing. Of course I realized I didn't care if 5700XT didn't have CrossFire because it didn't matter. DLSS also literally never was a consideration for me. Like it literally did not ever once factor into my decision going RDNA or Turing. So I'm just giving you my experience and why I made the decisions I made and never regretted it, which I soon came to realize I'd absolutely have had buyer's remorse for spending $200 more on a 2070 super. 

The one last thing to really emphasize: nVidia software sucks. It's to the point I'd be really sore about getting a RTX 4070 if I had to let go of my Adrenalin 2020. It's just so damn good. So nVidia also needs to at least pretend to care about their software. This is something that baffled me about Jay to no end which is why the hell he was using MSI Afterburner on any RDNA/RDNA2 card. Using MSI Afterburner feels like running Windows 8.1 to me.

text:
First off the only reason I'm on a vega 64 is because I can't find any gpus at a reasonable performance to cost ratio. See below,
I've been saying for years that if you match hardware it will perform significantly better. I am still gaming, VR and doing design work on a vega 64, water cooled, It can play games at 2160 at 60 fps with free sync. However my set up plays 1440p games closer to 200 fps than then it does 100 fps. Older games, well,  I have to limit the fps because they will run anywhere from 300-400fps to well over 2000 fps and you can hear the capacitors whining HardCore and it freaks me out! 
COMPONENTS
  -Cooler Master 1300 watt digital power supply, fully modular.
  -Gigabyte x570 master with my own custom water cooled chip set and vrm blocks.
  -AMD 3950x with full copper water block, no polycarbonate in my system. Running stock frequencies but water cooled with a full copper heat-exchanger .25" tubing, 8 pass,  24" tall by 12" wide by 4 inch deep to accommodate the .25" round copper tubes passing up and down from front to back not side to side, or up and down. Running 15 liters a minute, distilled water only.
-Water Lines are Goodyear 1/2" id. rubber tubing for high temperature car cooling systems as I used to build cars and this tubing works the best with zero maintenance for decades running glycol mix. (so it's good stuff) and super cheap, Napa Auto or Autozone or probably amazon at this point too.
  -16 - 140mm fans push and pull config. System total liquid is one gallon(3.75 liters)
  -2 ekwb d5 pumps running in push pull config. Honestly I did it for the balanced look, the second pump is just a waste of energy. There are no 90 degree corners in my system except for the internals of the water blocks.
  -1 liter reservoir for easy maintenance  
  - 64 gigs corsair icue ram
  - Vega 64 full copper waterblock running 150% power all the time
  - storage - 2 TB gen 4 corsair m.2
  - Samsung 680pro 512gb m.2  for jobs
  - Viewsonic VP3268 4k art monitor
  - Samsung 54inch 4k tv with freesync
  - WiFi 6 everywhere with hand made cat.7 cables

text:
It's been my main criticism of people like Linus for awhile, and why I actively simp for Jay like 90% of the time despite our at times varying taste, because Jayz is the best at thinking in terms of the average gamer who only buys his midgrade or lower stuff like once every 5-10 years, whereas you ask Linus to build the "absolute bottom of the barrel, cheap dirty piece of S&%# held together by dust and cobwebs" and...he puts a GTX 1070 in it. Like a few years after it was released.

To me the dirty cobweb budget PC is...a used GTX 970, in 2022, at best. Or, a used GTX 770 for the "cheapest held together by dust PC for 1080p" which I guarantee you is better than many have now. Like I'm looking at 770m laptops right now just because I want to save money on an added shitposting machine in bed that I can play at least some games on, not a real gaming machine like my desktop. 

Linus also needs to understand that not everybody wants to play Cyberpunk, and that for a whole hell of a lot of us gamers we're playing things like we see on Mandalore's and SsethTzeentach's channels from like 2009 or some indie gem made in 2016 or something like that, and not only often not playing those but outright thumbing our noses at AAA+ newly released games. Like I am literally on average playing a 5-7 year old game. It's a real thing that lot of these RTX 3070 owners are just playing like Rimworld or Factorio or something on it (or some cringey anime VN). 

So it's only really about expanding possibility, like having 16 core CPU in case sometime you ever make use of it, as opposed to our daily use of it, which in my case is a ~700+ title game libraries on Epic, GOG, and Steam that I just finished Vampire the Masquerade: Coteries and Kane and Lynch 2, and now am trying Call of Cthulhu. Right now, summer 2022, I played and beat Kane and Lynch 2. Out of 700 titles. So you can imagine how many missed triple A titles from 2012 and indie gems I am backlogging that can literally be played on a GTX 770 or R7 270x at 1080p all ultra no problem. 

Now consider not only that of those games probably only ~10% were made in the last 3-4 years, but that even of those 10%, like maybe a handful even have got raytracing, and you'll understand immediately why I don't give a shit about raytracing at all when it's literally 0.2% of my entire libraries having an RT option.

So to me it's really not only about "the struggle is real" but the frankly practical realistic terms that you gamers shouldn't feel bad on your potato because even those of us with decent hardware aren't even needing to use it that often and you can probably play like 90% of what I play on high with an RX 570 or lower. It's not just the struggle is real; the struggle isn't even needed.

text: I won a newegg shuffle and had the opportunity to buy gigabyte's rx 6700 xt 12gb eagle for $700 paired with an x570 aorus elite wifi for $220 (the exact same motherboard i already own). I will be selling the motherboard to a coworker for $160, so essentially I'll have paid $760 for it.  The card seems to have a much better cooler than the reference model, as well as rgb 2.0 which will sync nicely with my whole rig. Newegg's "bundles" are at face value annoying, but i guess it helped me secure a card, as more people try to win just the card than try to win the card and whatever other junk they pair with it that you don't need. I just completed a build last month and the only thing missing was, guess what? Yep, a video card. I have been using my old rx 580 4gb as a placeholder in my new build. I am just ecstatic that I will finally get to complete my build with a new card, it will be quite the upgrade from what I have. Most reviews for this card are very ho hum, which is kind of disheartening, but these reviews are comparing graphics cards as if we can actually enjoy a choice in the matter, but this is far from the reality of things... text:
tl;dr:
2:14 -- comparing 2 AMD "reference" spec cards vs 3 nVidia "Founders Edition" top-bin-GPU spec cards is not a Fair or Equal comparison.....??
EVEN to make comparisons to the 6700 XT . . .
WHY Would Anthony @AnJYoun Young risk the LONG-STANDING GREAT (_impartial_!?) REPUTATION of LTT this way???
QuickRef LTT 25 Feb 2021 3060 vid, 2min+, re: 1060 "Founders Edition" vs "reference" == significant difference between FE & ref.
[ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kAJAViPWR_8&t=124s ]

Long Form:

Hello, I would be the FIRST to admit I'm still "always learning" when it comes to tech hardware, and in that context, I will ALWAYS want to ASK A FAIR QUESTION to seek CLARITY.  ...and I have LONG TRUSTED that @Linus Tech Tips ALWAYS seeks to be FAIR with its information presentation.

(I'm fully aware that SOME people may feel inclined to JUMP DOWN MY THROAT for my Q, but... here's to hoping that the GREAT ADMIRATION & RESPECT I have for Linus & his team's work over MANY years is still evident here.)

2:14 -- In THIS video (above), you've lined up FIVE (5) cards: *2 AMD "Reference", and 3 nVidia "Founders Edition" cards.*  =)

BEFORE I GO ON with my Question, I'd just like to step back about THREE WEEKS to the *3060 REVIEW of 25 Feb 2021.*  
Most specifically, just past the 2min mark, where the "current" (Feb'21) 3060 pricing is compared to the 1060's historic pricing, adjusted for inflation.  Here's a direct link (please everyone watch at least 15sec):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kAJAViPWR_8&t=124s

There, its established (through price) that a "Founders Edition" 1060 nVidia card was (obviously/sensibly) more expensive than a "reference" 1060.  Typically -- and PLEASE DO correct me if I'm wholly off-base here? -- "more expensive" with GPUs DOES (most often*) mean "better spec", right?
AND . . is it NOT correct that "Founders Edition" cards are ALWAYS BETTER SPEC for that model of GPU?  with HIGHER boost clock speeds?
AND . . . that "reference" is the MINIMUM required hardware spec for a card build, e.g. base spec guidelines for AIB partner manufacturers?
PLUS . . . "Binning" of GPU chips is WIDELY understood to occur, right?

OK ... back to my question on THIS video.

Are there no "reference" versions of nVidia's 2080, 3060, and 3070 to put against the "reference" AMD 5700 and 6700 you used..?  O_O 

..because, unless I TOTALLY misunderstand, what Anthony @AnJYoun Young has done here has been -- let's be Fair / Honest here -- at least a little bit deceptive:  taking FOUNDERS EDITION (best-bin GPUs on reference-design) nVidia cards and putting them against REFERENCE (min spec) AMD cards APPEARS to unfairly allow nVidia cards an advantage in test-bench results, which goes to either (a) making nVidia results appear inflated, or (b) making AMD results appear diminished -- because it's then not an Oranges to Oranges comparison.  More like .. Oranges to Tangerines.  O_O 

(( .. and at 2:37, it becomes clear that perhaps picking a NON-"Reference" 5700 XT - one with higher GPU clocks / Boost clocks - would make for a more "feasible" / functional comparison with its next-gen 6700 XT, by "giving it a chance"?
I mean, why not -- the other 3 cards are ALL FOUNDERS EDITION spec..!!))

*THANK YOU..!!*

(Secondary Q:
Will he do a FRESH video with 2080, 3060, and 3070 REFERENCE edition nVidia cards, against the AMD 5700 & 6700 references?)  (Not likely..!?)

YES, I fully expect that my Question is "contentious" enough that Green Team members will want my head.  Time (and comment responses) will tell, I guess, how "cool" heads prevail . . or not.  ;)
author: @Grayson_Phoenix

text:
So, A.Y. , absent any replies - (& no troll harassment either, thank you) - my point is VALIDATED .. (not REFUTED . . in all this time).

The comparison made (2 "reference" spec cards vs 3 "Founders Edition" cards) is a FLAWED COMPARISON, and therefore UNFAIRLY MIS-REPRESENTS / MALIGNS one manufacturer's products as incorrectly sub-par to the other's.

It is NOT - as was claimed at 2:28 - a "fair fight". O_O

NOWHERE in this video is any purposeful reason for this mentioned; no follow-up has been made to CLARIFY the error, either.
No NEW video has been made to address / own up to this mistake.  No "Pinned comment" to correct/address this...

I don't care "what team" you're on (Green or Red, or even Blue) -- this is not a "fanboy rant" (how immature) -- an ERROR of comparison can lead to viewers being potentially MISLED, with INCORRECT INFORMATION, and that is just WRONG.

I TRUST @LinusTechTips for HIGH QUALITY tech info, and it's just really disappointing that Linus allows his name to be attached to this.

Again, if I've happened to somehow MISS something GLARINGLY OBVIOUS as to why the 2 "Reference" cards ARE "fairly comparable" to the 3 "Founders Edition" cards, please DO tell me -- I can accept when I'm wrong, and maybe Learn a thing or two.

text:
LTT could be the channel that solidifies testing quality over pure FPS, as upscaling+RIS can be used for AMD already, Super resolution will be later, and Nvidia has DLSS. Slow motion video footage on different techniques side by side, zoomed footage, zoomed slow motion footage, because that's the only way to test thoroughly and let the audience come to the conclusions about quality.

Screenshots favor DLSS heavily, fast movement and turns favor upscaling. And nobody knows about Super resolution.  If LTT manages to deliver the best testing methods for quality based assessments, then it solidifies it's status when it comes to testing GPUs. I don't know if any other channel could really pull that off, hopefully someone does, because it's important and will get more and more important.

Good quality comparison forces companies to focus on both quality and performance. Thus it will benefit the customers the most.
author: @juzujuzu4555

text:
Who buys mid range GPU for productivity workloads? Why these are tested instead of games? The amount of time these GPUs are used for gaming is 10 to 50 times more than what they are used for rendering.
Testing 7 games and 7 rendering etc. software, though Specviewperf itself consists of 8 different software really, seems like crazy way to test graphics cards. With 7 games the variance is just ridiculous, especially with this generation where Ampere has double FP32 per core and RDNA 2 has infinity cache and quite a lot of other changes too.

Sure there are lots of other reviews to look, but as the biggest tech channel LTT should really be the one that tests hardware properly. You could also be the channel that solidifies testing quality over pure FPS, as upscaling+RIS can be used for AMD already, Super resolution will be later, and Nvidia has DLSS. Slow motion video footage on different techniques side by side, zoomed footage, zoomed slow motion footage, because that's the only way to test thoroughly and let the audience come to the conclusions about quality.

Screenshots favor DLSS heavily, fast movement and turns favor upscaling. And nobody knows about Super resolution.  If LTT manages to deliver the best testing methods for quality based assessments, then it solidifies it's status when it comes to testing GPUs. I don't know if any other channel could really pull that off, hopefully someone does, because it's important and will get more and more important.

Frankly for anyone 1080p and under, you literally don't need much as you think. You don't need or notice 144fps, 90fps is fine even 75 in many games, it's really about frametimes not average fps anyway, and like over 90% of games are made for around GTX 970/GTX 1060/RX 480 recommended spec anyway. So a 1060 or 980 or RX 570 is perfectly fine for gaming. I wish it was clearer to gamers that a behemoth like 6900XT or 3090 was only needed for AAA games at 4k because even a 5700XT or 2070s can do 4k no prob on older titles, and anything more than 3060 or 6600 is basically just 1440p or 4k. Obviously if you have a 900p monitor, even a 980 is overkill most of the time even on new titles.

text:
High demand products or services that are limited in quantity should have an account/person/financial set up before release. When it goes on sale (whether it be graphics cards, concert tickets or any other thing that scalpers snatch up) he would log in and make the purchase (abiding by the limit) but even if you were first there would be no guarantee you get the product. Before determining who product is shipped to, the aforementioned account/person/financial information would be cross-referenced with all other purchasers. Any multiple addresses, names, financial institutions, IP addresses, etc for a particular purchaser would invalidate all their requested purchases. In the case of graphics cards, you as a person, along with any addresses you may be tied to and any financial accounts tied to that person will only get the number limited.
No Dad, Mom, brother, sisters, cousins, friends, etc allowing you to use their name and address while you pay for it.  
If a pending sale matches any other sale using the above criteria would instantly invalidate all purchases and with a manual review could mean a permanent ban from these types of purchases.

text:
That's a shame, especially with how well the 6800xt I borrowed did for me while I had it.  I didn't do benchmarks as I did them mostly useless.  I used it working in 3D software and both Unreal and Unity for real time rendering while setting up scenes.  I've only managed to get a 3070 for a short time I preferred the 6800xt in that case.

It's important to note I don't care about fps really.  Even with real time rendering I'm just setting up and scenes for a still render.  I use the engines to stream line my cg "photography" hobby and for creating scenes for renders to use in a possible comic pipeline.  As long as I can use the software within reason, having the extra VRAM has more value than raw power to an extent.  I really want to test a 3080 to see how it handles lighting/ray tracing in comparison.  From what I've seen it performs better but hits a point of diminishing returns once you get a quality threshold. text:
I'm not a fanboy of anybody or anything (I have Intel, nvidia and AMD products,  for example. I like Linux, Windows and Mac OS, Photoshop and Painter, etc). And about famous guys/women, they can make mistakes as well, they're just persons (I can totally admire people who makes mistakes! I don't love the mistakes, but they wouldn't be people if they would not make them!).    But besides doing a comment-meme (and that ain't bad)  there are some objective factors to praise Anthony (I would do so with any person in life, maybe only think of it, not saying it out loud, tho) : 

Calm voice and good tone, which is essential for complex matters and long format. Good writing (he's the writer of the videos he hosts, and of many other hosts, as he is very savvy in many and very varied tech matters), which is just as important to get people hooked. This leads to another strength : he knows how to explain stuff clearly (part of the reason to keep the viewer's attention). He knows the right pace and changes of tone to not bore anyone (interested in tech, that is). He is very savvy on Linux, video cards, systems in general. This last point already puts him way over many "youtube stars", whose stardom is mostly related to way more random/less valuable stuff, just looks, mere charisma, or pure histrionic overacting, etc. He's quite valiant in picking new ideas/projects. Like that emulation project for a hackintosh-ish of the Mac Pro on Linux. The man has also this good vibe that most people is able to detect (not everybody can , though). He's not a deity or something, just a very cool guy. I'm very glad he's having something at home to make some exercise, as my 4 uncles had problems related to overweight, and it did not end well.  But there's absolutely no need to keep pointing that out in every single thread and every single video, as we know he's aware and taking action about it. You're not telling him something he does not know. At this point, extra mentions of it (often disrespectfully) is a bit of bullying,  IMO.

text:
I'm not. I hate eceleb crap and it's one of the reasons I'm almost perpetually logged out of YT(well that and I passionately despise Google. I've used Bing and Firefox for ages by now and if I had the seed money I'd invest in starting a FreeVid kind of alternative video hosting channel, back to the way YT used to be, back before dipshits like markiplier or the puddingpie guy). 

No hate on Anthony, we all love tech shrek, but I was irritated enough by the tech review to actually log in. 3:04 my dudes, 3:04. If you're going to dub in a voiceover piece over video benchmarks, please make sure the words actually match the point you are making. It was up just long enough to notice it, and skipped entirely like "nevermind what is behind the curtain." 

My overall impression from seeing this video is just more of the same we all already know: if you're doing professional video editing nVidia is helpful, and nVidia does RT better if there's any games you play that have RT. Meanwhile as we also already know all the RTX cards' performance to value is complete ass, and part of the problem with most tech reviewers other than Jay is they're used to the shiniest, newest, highest end stuff as a matter of course, and so don't account for either tech noobs or people with modest incomes where budget matters.

 In that regard, if you were building a PC in 2020 you went with AMD GPU/CPU because their performance was better. If your budget is limited in any way at all, then the flagship card is totally irrelevant. It's about how fast is your dollar. 2070s was horribly bad performing in that regard, with 2080ti being possibly one of the worst GPU deals I've seen in over a decade. Linus' team frequently forgets things like this and that is why I like Jayztwocents better than possibly anyone, because he actually cares about his viewers, and talks to them as consumers, in a way LTT usually does not, because LTT basically amounts to a product showroom for high end hardware. Ampere similarly was a massive fail because AMD got its shit together in the GPU department, they just needed to lower prices by maybe $20 to make the contrast starker. The 6800 vs 3070ti showcases the worst value difference, which is exactly why nVidia went after everybody on youtube to try and push their proprietaryTM gimmick or marketing point. 

tl;dr So while this video is more of the same what everyone knows, it was edited really poorly to get their point across, which as a viewer I clearly can see as just a gamer the 6700XT isn't a bad deal at all, given the assumptions we already all know that tl;dr if you care about RT more than anything else, or do certain professional video work, you'll go with nVidia, if you want raw gamer performance to value of your overall budget including cooling and PSU, you're considering AMD.

text: If you recall, the GTX 1070 was a gpu based on the 1080, but with 25% of the cores etched off by laser along with a few board changes. Why would Nvidia waste perfectly good 1080 chips for 1070s when they already made them? The answer is that those chips weren’t perfectly good; they had imperfections like some cores didn’t work or didn’t operate at the standard of the 1080. They could repurpose their inventory of “dead” 1080s. I think that’s what AMD and Nvidia are doing again. I think they have a huge shortage of silicon and are trying to make the most of it. Scaling up production enough to meet the current demand would leave them screwed once demand died down again and they’d probably lose money on it once newer processes came out. We are at their mercy but honestly I’d be blaming the bots and scalpers... I see dozens of new GPUs for sale on craigslist, ebay, fb marketplace, etc.. The scalpers have destroyed the market. The sellers really should have introduced some kind of 1 card 1 customer policy (maybe make it monthly or whatever) and used an identity checking service to enforce it, but maybe some said that would be too far and who cares as long as the cards get sold, right? I dunno. I don’t think we should be upset at the gpu companies though, it’s gotta make the engineers doing their jobs feel bad.

text:
MSRPs should be brought in line with market value. People who think manufacturers have the authority to assign value to these cards are naïve. Value is subjective, and believing you are entitled to these products at MSRP is childish. If you don't want to empower scalpers then put your prices in line with the real market value. Who am I kidding, if they did that everyone would call them "greedy capitalists" even though doing so would be beneficial to consumers. If  retail prices were more in line with real value (I would even argue aiming to price a bit above market value would be best due to extreme demand) , scalpers would have no incentive to hoard, cards would be more available (albeit more expensive), but the additional money would be going to the manufacturer which you better believe means better products in the future, or could even be used to ramp up production to meet demand, instead of being syphoned off by scalpers.

Most people fail to realize the dilemma with scalpers is 100% within the power of manufacturers to eliminate, but they do nothing about it, and instead egg on the criticism of scalpers. Probably due to what I said above, if they did they would be derided for being "greedy" (even though they are simply reacting to market conditions) so instead they use this scalper shield to catch all the hate.
author: @UHDE0

text: Also, I just read a proposal for manufacturers to simply auction off supply themselves which I think is an excellent solution. Drop the silly notion of MSRP altogether and let the market discover the true value, while also minimizing or even eradicating any incentive for scalpers, so all of the profit goes straight to the manufacturer, as it should.

You seem to be misinterpreting the graph. 

The 6700xt is from their testing 102.6% the performance of a 3060TI.

text:
It's has high TDP because AMD decided to make small chip with very high clock speeds rather than bigger chip with lower clock speeds. Advantage of this is lower cost because each wafer yields more chips plus with limited wafer numbers that's also more chips. Unlike nvidia's 3060ti/3070 which has MSRP $100 under what AIBs can deliver, AMD has better cost structure and AIBs can actually hit MSRP(ofc this irrelevant right now and next 4 months). Also 6800 is not really a 3070 competitor, Navi21 is just too big chip and expensive. AMD cannot make many of them. 6700XT is not much expensive to make than 3060 12GB variant, mostly needs beefier cooler.

About mining, actual TDP has very little relevance if card is a good mining card or not. Every card's core gets downclocked and undervolted to minimum possible without hurting performance to save power consumption. With Ethereum, it's all about GPU memory performance so there a lot of room. For example 220W+ 5700XT's can be run at 140W with overclocked memory + undervolted&downclocked core while increasing mining performance from stock settings. What actually makes RDNA2 not that great mining cards is their cache+narrow memory bus. 6700XT is significantly worse at ETH mining than 5700XT, it's about same as 5600XT or 3060(all have 192bit GDDR6). Old Radeon7 is still clearly best AMD mining card ever produced.

About availability, market needs to cool down right now, any card able to mine(more than 4GB VRAM) are bought by miners with ridiculous overprices. They will buy 6700XTs too because there's no better cards on shelves. Only thing keeping cards on stock is very high pricing, it takes away profitability. ETH price has peaked, it should start to slide down towards summer. ETH difficulty has increased 60% from beginning of the year(miners get 60% less ETH per MH/s) and in July a fork is coming which reduces rewards from mining. There will a lot of amateur miners jumping of the train by then.

Nvidia released their card 3 weeks ago - both companies knew fully well that no one would be able to actually buy their cards, and there can be no doubt that YOU knew that no one would be able to buy the cards. Both releases are paper launches.

So why is AMD the only one that gets attacked for it?

I keep hearing Linus saying that he doesn't get why people claim he's shilling for Company A or Company B, but the three videos on Nvidia's RTX 3060 release and AMD's RX 6700XT are picture perfect examples of why people make these claims. It is, after all, hard to look at those three videos and conclude that LMG are not playing favourites.

text:
@logirex  to be fair, based on last years financials none of these were paper launches.

Incredible that we can have a year full of articles and images of mining farms in China popping up left and right to the point where we're seeing laptop mining farms now and everyone just ignores it and calls them paper launches.  

It's also quite entertaining watching everyone getting all upset that GPUs are creeping up in price as if things like more GDDR6 somehow being the same cost as less GDDR5 or as if prices should remain static in a market with supply chain disruptions - materials and distribution - and extremely high demand.  I know this will piss some people off but I genuinely do not understand how GPUs have managed to stay so cheap since the GTX 10 series and RX580's.  

And this is just as dumb as the "Should nVidia stop making the 3060" video.  Yea, I want a 3080, too, but I'm also not so self absorbed as to pretend like the low tier cards arent the market.

Yea, it sucks but AMD didnt just decide yesterday that they were going to drop a new card.  This could have been in the works for a year or two, and as a publicly traded company they have a fiduciary duty to investors meaning they couldn't spend all that money on R&D, tooling and manufacturing just to not release the product because crybaby gamers got some hurt feels.

However since August this happend: PC started crashing and then i called my pc technician. He saw that 2 of the 3 fans of GTX 970 were burned so he ordered 3 new fans from a shop in China. To stop the card from overheating and reduce someshow the overheat i downclocked it with MSI afterburner. It stopped crashing and i temperature was reduced to 75C from 87C. Yesterday he finaly came with the new fans. After 3 motnhs of it working with just one fan and reduced clocks. So installed the fans the temperature while not gaming went down to 32 c from 49c and during gaming it went doen to 48c crom 75. However when i swithcied the clocks back to normal pc started crashing. I talked with him today and he said that this means that the card started dying due some damaged it got during these 3 months working and overheating.
